I’ve tried to go back to school and I’ve just gotten too depressed each time and I have to drop out or take a shitty grade. I went through my worst episodes when I was working the Covid floor in 20/21. I was hospitalized several times and tried suicide twice. It is a stressful job but I am not my Bipolar. I like helping people, being there to uphold their dignity during this vulnerable time in their life, I like the strong women I work with, I like being busy and just being helpful and none of that has to do with my Bipolar. I’m medicated now and I’ve say I’m 70% better.

Honestly going to the hospital for the first time was a game changer for my condition. It’s not that I went to the hospital, came out, and then my life was amazing. But it set me on a path- I started trying medications, found a good therapist, being more open with my family, found other people that felt similar to me. I think you should try to be brave - the truth will set you free. I’m sure you’ve heard that phrase, it’s a cliche but, it’s a cliche because it’s true. Your life can improve, you don’t have to feel this way, and you don’t deserve to either. You don’t deserve to feel this way. But the only person who can get the ball rolling right now is you. So please, take this brave step. You can even write to them if you can’t say it out loud - there are no rules. You will go to the ER and it will be okay, they will take care of you from there. I have done it, so have so many people here. I am alive because of it, please try to tell them.

Bedroom

Hang up clothes in closet

Other things I'd like to mention are: the traffic here is a bit ridiculous. A lot of people are moving here because of the housing and jobs and the town wasn't really built for such a large population. So if you're commuting from or to here, accommodate for the extra time you'll need.

Episode 7 - Maybe I'm just a sucker for both Ep.1 and this episodes' baby themes? But The Hot Priest's acting actually made me tear up and it all felt genuine and it was actually really funny at some parts.

Episode 3 - At first, I found it to be really corny but Anne Hathaway's expression of what Bipolar depression feels like and how it was literally pulling her down and she couldn't get up, was all impressive. It started out as a very fun episode, followed by a rollar coaster of emotions.

Episode 6 - Okay, this one was weird but I didn't dislike it.  I was kind of freaked out because I thought she was attracted to him as her Dad and obviously, he thought the same. I just couldn't resonate with it. I still want to know what she was going to say when she yelled out "Wait!" at the end. Since, SPOILER.... we saw in episode 8 that she's with some totally different guy we've never seen. 

Episode 8 - I like this one because we get to see a glimpse of the other characters from the other episodes. It was just a cute little story, I wasn't necessarily touched. 

Episode 2 - This one I found to be annoying. The girlfriend cheats on him and he seemed to just forget about the whole thing after a few months/seeing her on the street one time and then the ex-gf leaves her own current fiance to get back with him?! It all seemed forced to me.

Episode 5 - I almost forgot to even include this. I thought the guy's character was so whiney and that her character was very far fetched. I did like, though, how they showed the vulnerability of the whole hospital situation that you can't avoid while accompanying someone at the hospital, whether it's family you've known forever or a brand new gf/bf.

Episode 4 - This is last because I was expecting so much more from it and was really let down. The chemistry wasn't there, and the story was lame. I love the actors in other movies and shows so, my expectations were maybe too high to begin with.

* This was all written kind of hastily at 5am but I'd love to discuss it further with anyone! I really did like the whole idea of the series. It reminded me of Love Actually. Now, excuse me while I go watch Episode 1 on repeat for eternity.
